evidence.title: Cedar County pauses solar, wind, data center projects for one year
evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 8, 2026 adoption, scope (solar, wind, battery storage, data centers), 25-kW exemption, six-month extension option, and the legal questions raised about the county's authority.
evidence.quote: Commissioners imposed the moratorium on September 8. It applies to larger new solar, wind, battery-storage and data-center developments outside city limits. Small on-site systems and existing projects are exempt. ... Commissioners can also extend the moratorium once for up to six additional months.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-08-23 (Ralls County Commission, signed at a Sunday courthouse meeting per WGEM's same-day report and Muddy River News)
new_candidates.legal_basis: Ralls County Commission order/moratorium, signed by all three commissioners 2026-08-23, halting economic-development applications related to data centers until 2027-09-01.
new_candidates.trigger: Commissioners moved after learning (from a tenant's report and, separately, from the county's electric cooperative) that a property owner along Mo. Highway 19 near Center may be negotiating to sell roughly 53 acres to a data center company; commissioners said they wanted time to study the issue before any project could be 'grandfathered in.'
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; halts economic-development applications related to data centers until 2027-09-01. Commissioners canceled a planning-and-zoning public hearing that had been scheduled for September and say they intend to let county voters decide on data centers, hopefully via an April ballot measure; no company has yet formally contacted the county about a project.
new_candidates.affected_projects: A possible data center project near Highway 19 east of Center, MO; the property owner reportedly received an offer to purchase roughly 53 acres, and the same prospective operator applied to the Ralls County Electric Cooperative for service, but no formal application or land purchase had been confirmed to the county as of the reporting reviewed.
new_candidates.outcome: Facing intense public pressure after residents learned of a possible data center land deal, the three Ralls County commissioners bypassed a planned September planning-and-zoning public hearing and signed a one-year moratorium on data center/economic-development applications, running through Sept. 1, 2027.

evidence.title: Around 100 residents voice displeasure with potential data center at meeting in Ralls County
evidence.supports: Same-day report confirming the moratorium was signed at the Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026 courthouse meeting.
evidence.quote: At 8 a.m. on Sunday, around a hundred Ralls County residents poured into the courthouse for a meeting regarding a potential data center in the county. ... A moratorium was also signed putting a hold on the project for at least one year.

evidence.title: Ralls County Commissioners place moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the specific end date (Sept. 1, 2027), that commissioners bypassed the planned September planning-and-zoning hearing, and background on the triggering land-sale report.
evidence.quote: The moratorium halts economic-development applications until September 1, 2027, giving the County time to study the issue and develop regulations.

evidence.title: Ralls County data center moratorium in place, commissioners want voters to have their say
evidence.supports: Confirms all three commissioners signed the one-year moratorium and that a planning-and-zoning public hearing on the topic was canceled as a result; commissioners want a public vote, hopefully in April.
evidence.quote: It ended with the commissioners signing a one-year moratorium on economic development projects and data centers. ... 'Yes, vote from all three of the Ralls County commissioners,' said Lake.

evidence.title: Ralls County, Mo. mulling over moratorium on data centers
evidence.supports: Background on the originally planned Sept. 16, 2026 planning-and-zoning hearing, which was canceled once commissioners went ahead and adopted the moratorium directly.
evidence.quote: UPDATE: Zoning meeting scheduled for September 16, at the Ralls County Courthouse in New London is canceled after commissioners went ahead and voted for a moratorium
